chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from al-Walīd ibn Ṣabīḥ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The blood-money for the Salūqī dog is forty dirhams. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded that, that he should pay its compensation to Banū Judhaymah.

key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the dog, the animal for which compensation is discussed
key_terms.دِيَةُ: financial compensation due for loss or injury
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, cited as the source of the ruling
key_terms.لِبَنِي جُذَيْمَةَ: to Banū Judhaymah, the people to whom the compensation was to be paid

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for a Salūqī dog in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the compensation due for killing or damaging a Salūqī dog, fixing its diyyah at forty dirhams. It also attributes this ruling to an order of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله concerning payment to Banū Judhaymah, indicating a prophetic precedent in matters of compensation.
